import pandas as pd


def _null_safe_eq(a, b):
    a_na = pd.isna(a)
    b_na = pd.isna(b)
    if a_na and b_na:
        return True
    if a_na or b_na:
        return False
    return a == b


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    dim_store = inputs["dim_store"].copy()
    stg_store_full = inputs["stg_store_full"].copy()
    batch_control = inputs["batch_control"].copy()

    # batch date
    b = batch_control["batch_date"].iloc[0]

    # Distinct snapshot rows
    S = stg_store_full[["store_id", "region", "format"]].drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

    # Current rows in dim_store
    is_current_mask = dim_store["is_current"] == 1
    current = dim_store[is_current_mask].copy()

    # Safety: if duplicate current rows per store_id existed, treat each independently
    # (legacy assumes at most one current row per store_id).
    current_by_store = current.set_index("store_id", drop=False)

    current_ids = set(current["store_id"].tolist())
    stg_ids = set(S["store_id"].tolist())

    closed_due_to_change = set()
    new_rows = []

    for _, s in S.iterrows():
        sid = s["store_id"]
        if sid in current_ids:
            c = current_by_store.loc[sid]
            # In case of duplicate index entries (shouldn't normally happen), take first
            if isinstance(c, pd.DataFrame):
                c = c.iloc[0]

            region_diff = not _null_safe_eq(c["region"], s["region"])
            format_diff = not _null_safe_eq(c["format"], s["format"])

            if region_diff or format_diff:
                closed_due_to_change.add(sid)
                new_rows.append({
                    "store_id": sid,
                    "region": s["region"],
                    "format": s["format"],
                    "eff_start_date": b,
                    "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                    "is_current": 1,
                })
            else:
                # no-op
                pass
        else:
            # brand-new or reactivated store
            new_rows.append({
                "store_id": sid,
                "region": s["region"],
                "format": s["format"],
                "eff_start_date": b,
                "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                "is_current": 1,
            })

    closed_due_to_missing = current_ids - stg_ids

    all_closed_ids = closed_due_to_change | closed_due_to_missing

    # Apply closing updates to dim_store: only to current rows whose store_id is in all_closed_ids
    out = dim_store.copy()
    close_mask = out["is_current"].eq(1) & out["store_id"].isin(all_closed_ids)
    out.loc[close_mask, "eff_end_date"] = b
    out.loc[close_mask, "is_current"] = 0

    # Append new rows
    if new_rows:
        new_df = pd.DataFrame(new_rows, columns=[
            "store_id", "region", "format", "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date", "is_current"
        ])
        out = pd.concat([out, new_df], ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure column order and types
    out = out[["store_id", "region", "format", "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date", "is_current"]]
    out["store_id"] = out["store_id"].astype("int64")
    out["is_current"] = out["is_current"].astype("int64")
    out["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(out["eff_start_date"])
    out["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(out["eff_end_date"])

    return {"dim_store_out": out.reset_index(drop=True)}
